conventions.convention: The lattice is Γ = Z^d with d ≥ 1 and finite on-site dimension q ≥ 1. Infinite states are bounded positive normalized complex-linear functionals on the norm-completed local matrix algebra, with finite-region density matrices; no global infinite tensor-product density matrix is selected.

SI energy coefficients are in joules, temperature T > 0 is in kelvins, β = 1/(k_B T) is in inverse joules, and the physical-time evolution is conjugation by exp(itH/ℏ). The KMS strip has width βℏ seconds, lower boundary ω(Aα_t(B)), and upper boundary ω(α_t(B)A).

Local projective outcomes have adopted Born probabilities ω(P), and KMS is adopted as the physical equilibrium criterion. Neither adoption asserts relaxation, material identification, apparatus realization, or experimental confirmation.

Finite Hamiltonians have free boundaries: only interaction terms whose entire support lies in the finite region are included. The Ising Hamiltonian has negative field and pair terms, dimensionless Z_i eigenvalues ±1, and each unordered internal pair counted once.

Van Hove sequences consist of finite nonempty regions with cardinalities tending to infinity and negligible inner boundaries at every fixed integer width, using minimum max-coordinate distance to the lattice complement. The pressure p is dimensionless log-partition per site; f = −β⁻¹p is free energy per site, not mechanical pressure.

The entropy-density construction assumes spatial translation invariance, Countable Choice and full AC, uses positive-integer cubes Q_L = {0,…,L−1}^d, and adopts 0 log 0 = 0. The downstream dynamics and phase deductions explicitly do not use this separate AC-dependent clause.

The high-temperature influence inequality is strict. Two-dimensional coexistence instead assumes J > 0, zero field and βJ ≥ 2, equivalently T ≤ J/(2k_B). These are sufficient regimes, with no exact critical-temperature or extremality claim. Pressure secants are with respect to the longitudinal energy coefficient h and therefore carry a factor β.

load_bearing.statement: Defines the infinite spin state and ordered local correlations, SI primitive inputs and derived β, free-boundary finite Gibbs quantities, physical-time dynamics and KMS conventions. Under translation-invariant finite-range hypotheses it defines the van Hove pressure and free energy per site. Under spatial translation invariance, Countable Choice and full AC, it defines cube entropy density and the anchored-shape energy density.

The model assigns the Born probability ω(P) to a local projective-measurement outcome. For a physical equilibrium preparation at T > 0, it adopts that ω is a β-KMS state for the thermodynamic dynamics, with β = 1/(k_B T) and physical-time strip width βℏ seconds.

Under the adopted diagonal spin-1/2 model, Countable Choice and the stated finite-matrix interfaces: translation-invariant symmetric finite-range couplings and constant finite field give exactly one full-algebra β-KMS state when sup_i Σ_{j≠i} tanh(β|J_ij|) < 1; the uniform nearest-neighbor chain has exactly one at every positive temperature for finite J,h; the square-lattice nearest-neighbor ferromagnet at zero field and βJ ≥ 2 has two distinct translation-invariant KMS states with magnetizations bounded by ±m_*, where m_* = 1−2δ(βJ), δ(K) = (4/3)r⁴(5−4r)/(1−r)² and r = 3 exp(−2K). Its field-dependent cubic-box pressure exists, is nondifferentiable at zero, and has secants at least βm_* for every h > 0 and at most −βm_* for every h < 0.

Under the adopted spin interpretation, uniformly bounded finite-range interaction, Countable Choice and the stated finite-matrix C*-identity and state/density-norm interface, thermodynamic dynamics exists as a strongly continuous group of isometric *-automorphisms and has at least one β-KMS state for every fixed β > 0. With translation invariance, finite-volume dimensionless log-partition per site converges to the same finite limit along every stated van Hove sequence, and f_Φ = −β⁻¹p_Φ = −k_B T p_Φ.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact arbitrary-family choice assumption carried by the physical definition's entropy-density supplier. The other assigned deductions explicitly exclude use of that entropy clause.
Exact indexed-family choice assumption carried by algebra completion, thermodynamic dynamics, KMS existence and the classical-measure/quantum-phase supplier chains.

seams_checked.note: Compared the physical phase theorem with the diagonal interaction and the chain, high-temperature and coexistence KMS suppliers, and inspected their full-algebra KMS–DLR correspondence. Pair counting, energy signs, constant-field and translation hypotheses, strict influence bound, βJ ≥ 2 threshold, magnetization formula and β-weighted pressure secants agree. The physical page preserves the exclusions concerning transverse fields, criticality, extremality and empirical materials.

Compared the physical definitions and equilibrium prediction with the translation-invariant interaction, pressure theorem and stationary entropy-density lemma. The inner-boundary van Hove condition, free-boundary normalization, common pressure limit, anchored-shape energy sum and cube-entropy infimum agree. Full AC remains explicit for entropy, while pressure is restricted to translation-invariant finite-range interactions.
